speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your vertigo, can you describe exactly what triggers the spinning sensation, and does moving your head make it significantly worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the spinning sensation return if you lie down and turn your head to either side, or does it only occur when you move your head in a specific direction? I also need to know if you are experiencing any hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or neurological symptoms like double vision or slurred speech.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does changing your head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up, reliably reproduce the spinning sensation? Also, have you noticed any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or weakness in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or neurological symptoms like double vision or slurred speech? I need to rule out central causes or Meniere's disease.
